item.title: [MLB.com] All signs pointing to a dream Skubal-Miz showdown for NLCS Game 1
item.dc:creator: Max Ralph

item.content:encoded:
You get what’s shaping up to be pretty much the best pitching matchup you could ask for in Game 1 of the NL Championship Series.
The Dodgers announced Friday that Tarik Skubal will get the ball in Game 1 on Sunday, and while the Brewers haven't made anything official, they are in prime position to have ace Jacob Misiorowski on the mound. Both teams clinched their spot in the NLCS on Thursday, the Brewers with a 3-1 win over the Padres and the Dodgers with a 4-1 win over the Braves.
Misiorowski pitched just once in the series, throwing four innings of two-run ball in Game 1. Similarly, Skubal opened things against the Braves, going six innings with just one run allowed, and did not pitch again. Both should be well-rested.
The most realistic argument against a Skubal-Misiorowski duel lies in October superstar Yoshinobu Yamamoto, but the Dodgers righty pitched in Game 3 of the NLDS on Tuesday, meaning he’d start Sunday on just four days’ rest. He will pitch in Game 2 on Monday with a regular recovery that would make more sense.
We’ve seen great pitching in the 2026 postseason thus far and several marquee matchups: Cam Schlittler vs. Payton Tolle; Chris Sale vs. Jesús Luzardo; Max Fried vs. Sonny Gray; Gerrit Cole vs. Drew Rasmussen; Yamamoto vs. Sale.
If it happens, Skubal vs. Misiorowski will take the cake.
After some struggles late in the regular season, Misiorowski pitched behind an opener when he made his postseason debut a year ago, but he was effective in three appearances. He allowed only one run across seven innings in the NLDS against the Cubs, before striking out nine and yielding just one run in five innings against the Dodgers in the NLCS.
But this is not the same Miz in 2026. The flame-throwing 24-year-old finished the regular season with MLB bests in ERA (1.80), strikeouts (252), WHIP (0.80) and opponents’ batting average (.157). It was more than a breakout -- it was among the greatest pitching seasons in MLB history.
Misiorowski’s four-seam fastball topped out at 104.8 mph and averaged 101.2 mph against the Padres in the NLDS. With the adrenaline that is sure to be present on Sunday, who knows what eye-popping numbers he could put up.
As for Skubal, he won’t win a third consecutive Cy Young. But that won’t take away from the 2.72 ERA he posted in 26 starts, including a 2.61 mark after his blockbuster trade to the Dodgers. Remember, too, that Skubal missed 44 days in the summer after he needed surgery to remove loose bodies in his left elbow. There have been few signs of rust from that recovery.
Skubal’s strong playoff debut with the Dodgers was just more of what we’re used to from the southpaw. He made six postseason starts as a Tiger in 2024 and 2025 with a 2.04 ERA, never going shorter than six innings and allowing more than two runs just once.
The Brewers and Dodgers will already provide appointment viewing throughout the NLCS, a rematch of the 2025 NL pennant battle and a meeting of MLB’s top regular-season teams in 2026. Add in the potential bout of Misiorowski and Skubal in Game 1, and this series should get off to an awfully hot start.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Tarik Skubal starts for Dodgers in NLCS Game 1, Yoshinobu Yamamoto in Game 2

item.content:encoded:
Winning the National League Division Series in four games afforded the Dodgers the luxury of setting their starting rotation exactly the way they wanted for the next round. Tarik Skubal gets the ball in Game 1 of the National League Championship Series against the Brewers, with Yoshinobu Yamamoto in Game 2 to cover the first two games of the series in Milwaukee, manager Dave Roberts said via Zoom on Friday.
Skubal struck out seven in six innings in his win over the Atlanta Braves in Game 1 of the NLDS. This will be the fourth Game 1 start for Skubal, who has a 1.97 ERA in seven career postseason starts, with 63 strikeouts and seven unintentional walks in 45 2/3 innings, and he's lasted at least six innings in all seven starts.
Yamamoto added to his legend in Game 7 of last year's World Series, getting the final eight outs of Game 7 one day after starting and pitching six innings in Game 6. He's the only pitcher in postseason history to win five straight road appearances while allowing no more than one run in each game, a streak that began in Game 2 of last year's NLCS, also in Milwaukee.
Ahead of his NLDS start, Yamamoto expressed willingness to start on short rest or pitch of out of the bullpen if needed when asked.
"I'm going to get myself ready for any situation. If they want me to go out, then I go out," Yamamoto said, with interpreter Yoshihiro Sonoda. "But for me, just those are key things for me. Postseason is just focusing on the game right in front of me."
But this far, every one of Yamamoto's 86 MLB starts — including 10 in the postseason — have come with at least five days rest, and Game 2 comes with five days rest after his 10 strikeouts in seven innings on Tuesday in Atlanta. And starting Yamamoto in Game 2 of a best-of-7 series would allow him to also start in Game 6 on five days rest, while Games 1 and 3 starters would start in Games 5 and 7 on four days rest.
"It's more looking at how he's gotten his rest this year, and what gives him the best chance to pitch potentially two games, Games 2 and 6," Roberts said. "With the off days and the game schedule, that's probably the best way to manage it."

item.title: [Metro Philadelphia] Should the Phillies sign Randy Arozarena or Seiya Suzuki? - Metro Philadelphia
item.dc:creator: Cory Nidoh

item.content:encoded:
The Philadelphia Phillies will look to improve a roster that once again dealt with injuries and shortcomings, leading to an early exit in the postseason.
The two corner outfield spots are key areas Dave Dombrowski, Preston Mattingly and the front office will need to focus on, along with the bullpen.
Left field has been a platoon over the last two seasons, while the team has struggled to get typical corner outfield production from a right fielder since Nick Castellanos’ All-Star season in 2023, where he clubbed 29 home runs and drove in a career-best 106 runs.
Since 2021, the Phillies have had 26 different starters in left field, with Brandon Marsh, Kyle Schwarber and Andrew McCutchen getting the majority of the starts during that stretch.
Over in right field, the Phillies also penciled in 26 different names to patrol right field, with Nick Castellanos and Bryce Harper earning the lion's share.
Despite the upcoming free agent pool being quite shallow, Randy Arozarena and Seiya Suzuki are a pair of outfielders on the market that the Phillies should target that could provide stability for multiple seasons.
Entering his age 32 season next year (assuming there is a season), Arozarena could be an intriguing pickup for the Phillies. He was named an All-Star with the Seattle Mariners after slashing .281/.381/.484 with an .865 OPS. He hit 26 home runs and drove in 79 runs.
He posted a 151 wRC+ and 5.7 WAR.
Stacking him up to the hitters in the Phillies’ lineup this season, he would have ranked within the top five in AVG, OBP, SLG, OPS, HR and RBIs.
Arozarena is coming off essentially a career year. His triple slash line numbers represent career highs in a full season for the outfielder, and it could have been an outlier campaign for him.
Nonetheless, even his career numbers at .255/.350/.442 and .792 OPS, along with his ability to hit 20-plus homers in six straight seasons, warrant a phone call from the Phillies, who may need him more than any other team in the league.
He would provide much-needed pop from the right side of the plate, something this lineup has been missing for a few years. This season, the Phillies ranked 22nd in MLB in OPS and 28th in on-base percentage from their right-handed hitters.
He also has more speed on the basepaths than Suzuki, adding some athleticism to a Phillies lineup that can become station-to-station at times.
Defensively, he isn't great, but the Phillies need stabilizing bats in the lineup due to the consistent ebbs and flows this lineup has endured over the course of the last handful of seasons, especially come playoff time.
Perhaps the biggest selling point for Arozerena may not be what he does over 162 games, but what he's already done when the stakes are highest.
His postseason résumé gives him an element Suzuki simply doesn't have at the major league level—a proven ability to become a difference-maker when the calendar flips to October.
Arozarena has plenty of experience playing in big moments. He has played in 45 career postseason games, slashing .292/.380/.565 with a .946 OPS across 184 plate appearances. He also has hit 12 bombs in the playoffs and has a knack for the theatrics.
Bringing him in would more than likely mean Brandon Marsh would be traded. The veteran is not a platoon-type bat and would be an everyday plug-and-play-type offensive piece in the middle of the lineup.
He won't be cheap.
Coming off one of his best seasons offensively, he will more than likely command a contract north of $100 million.
While not young either, the Phillies may not have a choice but to add another player in his 30s into the mix to capitalize on the closing title window.
Suzuki, who will turn 33 late next season, would bring similar traits to the lineup that Arozarena would, but perhaps on a more consistent level.
This season, he slashed .270/.368/.473 with an .841 OPS to go with 26 homers, 86 RBIs and a wRC+ of 134.
His 81 walks and 5.1 wins above replacement were career watermarks. It also marked a fourth consecutive season that he posted an OPS north of .800 and third in the last four years, where it was .840 or better.
The outfielder has been a consistent middle-of-the-order bat during his tenure with the Chicago Cubs.
Since 2023, he has had at least 140 hits, 27 doubles, 20 home runs and 70 RBIs. He would be two seasons removed from his best campaign of his five-year big league career in 2025, where he posted career-best in home runs (32) and RBIs (103).
His 113 career home runs are the third-most home runs in Cubs' history, only behind Kris Bryant (138) and Hall of Famer Ernie Banks (136).
During that same stretch he has averaged 28 homers and 97 RBIs per 162-game season. He also averages 72 walks per season during that span, and his patient approach would go a long way for a Phillies lineup that has repeatedly had chase issues, especially in the postseason when it’s become magnified.
Suzuki owns a slightly better career walk rate (10.9%) compared to Arozarena (9.8%).
He’s also a significantly better defender and made major improvements in that department this season. His 14 defensive runs saved this season were good for 17th-best among all outfielders, as opposed to Arozarena’s -2.
The other caveat with Suzuki is that he would be a different type of signing for the organization.
Philadelphia historically has not ventured into signing top Japanese talent, whether directly from Japan or even once they become assimilated stateside in MLB.
Of course, it’s not easy to break into such a market when there is no prior history. Add the fact that the Los Angeles Dodgers have established themselves as the premier destination for Japanese stars looking to take their talents to the top league in the world; it makes it all that more difficult.
The Phillies recently tried their luck with Koyo Aoyagi, a right-handed pitcher the team signed to a minor league contract before the 2025 season. Aoyagi posted a 7.22 ERA between Double-A and Triple-A and never made it to the big league club.
Other examples include Tadahito Iguchi, who they traded for in 2007 and So Taguchi, who they signed after spending six seasons with St. Louis. Neither was the caliber player Suzuki is and is not a success story that the team could use as a recruiting pitch to some of the top players, like star third baseman Teruaki Sato, who plays for the Hanshin Tigers of the Nippon Professional Baseball League.
General manager Preston Mattingly reportedly took a trip overseas to observe the 27-year-old who could be making his way over to the United States.
The Phillies also shouldn’t just sign Suzuki to say they signed a Japanese talent.
However, the talent is there and Suzuki would stabilize right field, a position that has become a revolving door over the last few seasons.
Like Arozarena, Suzuki would command a multi-year deal northwards of $100 million after he signed a five-year, $85 million deal with the Cubs.
But for a Phillies team that has spent years searching for stability in right field since Bryce Harper moved to first base, Suzuki wouldn't be simply another expensive bat. He'd be a proven middle-of-the-order hitter who gets on base, provides above-average defense, and has demonstrated the kind of year-to-year consistency the position has lacked.
Both players certainly fit the needs of the Phillies and wouldn't be a bad starting point to fix this roster.

item.content:encoded:
Oct 8, 2026, 11:35 AM ET
New York Yankees impending free-agent first baseman/designated hitter Paul Goldschmidt has expressed a desire to keep playing at age 39 in 2027, according to Gary Phillips of the New York Daily News. It is unclear if the Yankees will make an effort to re-sign the former MVP and seven-time All-Star in the offseason. Goldy had a nice bounce-back campaign in 2026 in his 16th year in the big leagues after he hit just 10 homers and drove in 45 runs in 146 games in 2025 in his first year in pinstripes. In 105 regular-season games across 380 plate appearances this year, Goldschmidt hit .252/.313/.452 with a .765 OPS, 18 home runs, 52 RBI, and 44 runs scored for the Yankees. He went hitless in eight plate appearances with two walks and a run scored in four postseason games for New York this year. Goldschmidt is obviously no longer in his prime and is no longer an everyday player, but he should still attract interest across the league for his ability to hit lefties. In 183 plate appearances against southpaws in 2026, he hit .299 (47-for-157) with 11 of his 18 home runs and 24 RBI.--Keith Hernandez
Source: New York Daily News - Gary Phillips
More Recent News
Oct 8, 2026, 11:28 AM ET
Tampa Bay Rays closer Bryan Baker shut the door in his team's 4-3 win over the New York Yankees in Game 3 of the American League Division Series on Wednesday, pitching a scoreless ninth inning with two strikeouts. Baker was a key part of Tampa Bay's three-game sweep of New York, logging saves in all three games while allowing just one baserunner to reach. The 31-year-old emerged as one of the best closers in baseball during the regular season, recording a 1.44 ERA and 0.91 WHIP with 63 strikeouts and 41 saves across 62 1/3 innings (65 games). Heading into the American League Championship Series, Baker's dominance at the end of games gives Tampa Bay a significant advantage if it can get an early lead on its opponents.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Jakob Marsee Having UCL Repair With Internal Brace


Keith Hernandez




Oct 8, 2026, 11:24 AM ET
Miami Marlins outfielder Jakob Marsee (elbow) will get a UCL repair with an internal brace of his left elbow on Monday, according to Christina De Nicola of MLB.com. The estimated return-to-play timeline for Marsee is around six months. Marsee battled through elbow issues down the stretch in 2026 in his first full season in the majors with Miami. In his first taste of the big leagues in 2025, Marsee hit .292 (61-for-209) with five home runs, 33 RBI, 14 stolen bases, and 28 runs scored in 55 games and 234 plate appearances. In 155 games and 616 plate appearances this year, Marsee slashed .231/.348/.359 with a .706 OPS, 11 home runs, 41 RBI, 23 stolen bases, and 83 runs scored for the Fish. The 25-year-old former sixth-round pick by the San Diego Padres in 2022 from Central Michigan University has a very intriguing power/speed profile as an outfielder in all fantasy leagues, but his availability for Opening Day in 2027 could be in question, depending on how he fares during his rehab after going under the knife early next week.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com - Christina De Nicola
Oct 8, 2026, 11:21 AM ET
Milwaukee Brewers outfielder Garrett Mitchell had a big game in his team's 3-1, series-clinching win over the San Diego Padres in Game 4 of the National League Division Series on Wednesday. At the plate, Mitchell went two-for-four with a triple, an RBI, and a run scored. In the field, Mitchell robbed Padres third baseman Manny Machado of what would have been a game-tying two-run home run in the eighth inning. The 28-year-old Mitchell was finally able to stay mostly healthy in 2026, hitting .262/.354/.416 with 11 home runs, 65 RBI, 74 runs scored, and 14 stolen bases across 531 plate appearances in the regular season. He was productive in the NLDS as well, logging four hits, three runs scored, an RBI, and a stolen base across 15 at-bats.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Hagen Smith Opening Game 4 of ALDS on Thursday


Keith Hernandez




Oct 8, 2026, 11:15 AM ET
Chicago White Sox rookie left-hander Hagen Smith will serve as the opener in Game 4 of the American League Division Series on Thursday at home against the division-rival Cleveland Guardians, according to Scott Merkin of MLB.com. The 23-year-old former fifth overall pick in 2024 from the University of Arkansas made 18 appearances (only one start) in his major-league debut during the 2026 regular season, posting a nice 1.29 ERA (2.35 FIP) and 0.96 WHIP with 41 strikeouts and 16 walks in 28 innings pitched. The talented young southpaw has already thrown 6 1/3 innings in his first experience in the playoffs, too, allowing just one earned run on three hits while walking five and striking out six. He started Game 1 of the ALDS against Cleveland and threw 2 2/3 shutout innings with three walks and four strikeouts in the team's 3-0 victory before allowing a run with two walks and a strikeout in two-thirds of an inning in Wednesday's Game 3 loss. Smith will probably have a short leash as the White Sox try to close out the best-of-five series, with right-hander Erick Fedde potentially piggybacking Smith in Chicago. In three relief appearances against the Guardians during the regular season, Smith allowed two earned runs with six walks and eight strikeouts in 5 2/3 innings pitched.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com - Scott Merkin
Victor Mesa Jr. Homers in ALDS-Clinching Win


Will Brady




Oct 8, 2026, 11:14 AM ET
Tampa Bay Rays outfielder Victor Mesa Jr. was one of the stars of his team's 4-3 win in Game 3 of the American League Division Series over the New York Yankees, hitting a two-run home run off Yankees left-hander Max Fried. Mesa Jr.'s home run was his only hit of the night, but it gave the Rays a 4-2 lead in the sixth inning that they would ultimately never give back. Across 262 plate appearances in the regular season, Mesa Jr. hit .260/.327/.498 with 14 home runs, 34 RBI, 37 runs scored, and nine stolen bases. After starting the year in the minors, the 25-year-old has emerged as an everyday corner outfielder for Tampa Bay and provides another dynamic power/speed bat for the Rays. If Mesa Jr. can get hot, he could help power a deep postseason run.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 7, 2026, 10:01 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers closer Edwin Diaz picked up his second save in as many nights on Wednesday, pitching a scoreless ninth inning with a strikeout in his team's 4-1 victory over the Atlanta Braves in Game 4 of the National League Division Series. Diaz missed most of the 2026 regular season due to elbow and neck injuries. However, he's been dominant since returning from the injured list in mid-September. Diaz allowed just two baserunners while notching nine strikeouts in his final five innings pitched of the regular season, and he's now logged low-stress saves in each of his first two appearances of the playoffs. With Diaz rounding into form, Los Angeles' bullpen looks like a major strength heading into the National League Championship Series.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 7, 2026, 9:52 PM ET
Cleveland Guardians left-hander Foster Griffin was dominant in a bulk relief appearance in his team's 9-3 win over the Chicago White Sox in Game 3 of the American League Division Series on Wednesday. Griffin followed Cleveland opener Daniel Espino and allowed two hits and one earned run while striking out seven across 2 2/3 innings of work. The 31-year-old was used exclusively as a starting pitcher during the regular season, posting a 15-6 record with a 3.60 ERA, 1.21 WHIP, and 158 strikeouts across 172 2/3 innings (31 starts) split between the Guardians and the Washington Nationals. However, Griffin struggled mightily late in the year, pitching to a 5.05 ERA in the second half and a 6.87 ERA across 18 1/3 innings in September. If Griffin can rediscover his early-season form in a bullpen role, he could help Cleveland mount a comeback in the ALDS.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 7, 2026, 9:43 PM ET
Cleveland Guardians outfielder Jo Adell had a big night in his team's 9-3 victory over the Chicago White Sox in Game 3 of the American League Division Series on Wednesday, going 2-for-4 with a walk and three RBI. With the game tied 1-1 in the third inning, Adell put the Guardians ahead for good with a three-run triple off of White Sox left-hander Hagen Smith. Across 660 regular-season plate appearances split between the Guardians and the Los Angeles Angels, Adell hit .240/.298/.401 with 23 home runs, 94 RBI, 70 runs scored, and five stolen bases. He was better with Cleveland than he was with Los Angeles, posting a .740 OPS across 204 trips to the plate after the Guardians acquired him at the trade deadline. Adell has notched a couple of key hits for Cleveland in the ALDS and now has four RBI across the first three games of the series.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 7, 2026, 9:32 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder Andy Pages had the key hit in his team's 4-1 win over the Atlanta Braves in Game 4 of the National League Division Series on Wednesday, logging a go-ahead two-run single off Braves right-hander Robert Suarez in the seventh inning. Pages finished the game with two hits and two RBI in three at-bats. The 25-year-old was a critical piece of the Dodgers lineup during the regular season, hitting .274 with 23 home runs, 85 RBI, 75 runs scored, and 13 stolen bases. However, Pages struggled mightily during the Dodgers' run to the 2025 World Series, notching just four hits in 55 postseason plate appearances. After his big night on Wednesday, Pages has already logged four hits in just 15 plate appearances in the 2026 playoffs.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 7, 2026, 9:19 PM ET
Cleveland Guardians right-hander Cade Smith was lights out to secure his team's 9-3 victory over the Chicago White Sox in Game 3 of the American League Division Series on Wednesday. Smith entered the game in the eighth inning and recorded the final six outs, logging five strikeouts without allowing a single baserunner. The 27-year-old was one of the best closers in baseball during the regular season, pitching to a 1.95 ERA and 0.96 WHIP with 107 strikeouts and 41 saves across 74 innings (69 games). Smith has been dominant so far in the Division Series as well, as he's yet to allow a hit or a walk in his four innings of work. If Cleveland is going to mount a comeback in the series, it will likely need Smith to continue his dominance.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 7, 2026, 9:11 PM ET
Cleveland Guardians third baseman Jose Ramirez was one of the stars of his team's 9-3 victory over the Chicago White Sox in Game 3 of the American League Division Series. In five plate appearances, Ramirez recorded a double, a triple, a walk, two RBI, two runs scored, and a stolen base. With Cleveland leading 5-3 in the 8th inning, it was Ramirez's two-run triple that sealed the win for the Guardians and kept the series alive to see Game 4. The 34-year-old battled through injuries and underperformance in 2026, hitting .235/.320/.368 with 12 home runs, 53 RBI, 71 runs scored, and 37 stolen bases across 544 plate appearances. Ramirez also got off to a slow start in the postseason, going hitless in his first eight trips to the plate against the White Sox. If Cleveland is going to rally all the way back from two games down in the ALDS, it will need Ramirez to stay hot in Games 4 and 5.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Robert Gasser Starting Game 4 of NLDS Against Padres


Keith Hernandez




Oct 7, 2026, 8:08 PM ET
Milwaukee Brewers left-hander Robert Gasser will start for the Brewers in Game 4 of the National League Division Series on Wednesday night at Petco Park against the San Diego Padres, according to Brewers reporter Sophia Minnaert. It will be Gasser's first career postseason start after throwing 2 2/3 innings of relief in the playoffs for the Brew Crew last year. The 27-year-old southpaw went 5-5 on the season with a 3.87 ERA (4.24 FIP) and 1.19 WHIP with a career-high 103 strikeouts and 35 walks in 109 1/3 innings across 21 appearances (20 starts). The problem for Gasser is that he has not made a start in almost two weeks, so he could be a bit rusty. Manager Pat Murphy will surely have a short hook on the young left-hander as the Brewers look to close the best-of-five series out in San Diego. Gasser was outstanding down the stretch in 2026, allowing two earned runs or fewer in each of his last six starts, walking 12 and striking out 31 in 32 1/3 innings during that span. He did not face the Padres at all during the regular season, which could give him a bit of an advantage.--Keith Hernandez
Source: Sophia Minnaert
Mason Miller Back From the Paternity List for Game 4


Keith Hernandez




Oct 7, 2026, 8:03 PM ET
The San Diego Padres announced on Wednesday that they returned right-handed closer Mason Miller from the paternity list, taking the place on the National League Division Series roster of left-handed reliever Wandy Peralta. Miller blew a two-inning save in Game 2 of the series in Milwaukee against the Brewers and was then unavailable for the win in Game 3 at Petco Park on Tuesday night. It is great news for the Padres, who did not have left-handed high-leverage reliever Adrian Morejon on Tuesday due to a left-shoulder issue. The Padres had to go to Game 1 starter, right-hander Michael King, for the two-inning save with both Miller and Morejon unavailable. It is uncertain if Morejon will be able to pitch late in the game in another must-win contest on Wednesday in Game 4, but the Padres will at least have their stud closer back in the fold. The two-time All-Star was lights-out during the regular season, his first full season with the Friars, posting a 1.67 ERA (1.17 FIP), 0.900 WHIP, a career-high and league-high 38 saves, a career-high 129 strikeouts, and 26 walks in just 70 innings pitched. With their season on the line, expect manager Craig Stammen to be aggressive in his usage of Miller if Game 4 is close in the later innings, even though he showed command issues in the ninth on Sunday in Milwaukee.--Keith Hernandez
Source: San Diego Padres
Miguel Rojas Not Worried About Back/Hip Injury


Keith Hernandez




Oct 7, 2026, 12:28 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers veteran infielder Miguel Rojas (back, hip) said he felt some tightness in his left lower-back/hip area during a swing in Game 3 of the National League Division Series on Tuesday against the hosting Atlanta Braves before he was pulled mid at-bat, according to Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic. However, Rojas was not concerned about his availability for the rest of the series and going forward. Rojas probably will not be in the Dodgers' starting lineup for Game 4 of the series on Wednesday at Truist Park against Braves right-hander Tyler Mahle, but it sounds like he should be available off the bench. The 37-year-old Venezuelan infielder has made two starts so far in the NLDS against the Braves and has gone 1-for-4 with a double and a strikeout. He was hitless in three at-bats with a strikeout in Tuesday's Game 3 win before being replaced at second base by Tommy Edman. Rojas has mostly been a bench player for the Dodgers in his 13th year in the league (fourth with L.A.) in 2026, but he proved in last year's World Series that he is still capable of coming through in the clutch when needed. He hit .267 (60-for-225) with four homers and 23 RBI during the regular season.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Athletic - Fabian Ardaya
Oct 7, 2026, 11:57 AM ET
St. Louis Cardinals right-handed closer Riley O'Brien was a first-time All-Star in 2026 in his first full season as the team's closer, and he ended the year tied with San Diego Padres closer Mason Miller for the National League lead in saves (38) with a 4.08 ERA across a career-high 64 innings pitched. O'Brien also set a career high in appearances (66) in his first full year as a big-leaguer. He did not allow an earned run in his first 13 appearances of the year and ended the first half with a 3.43 ERA and a 7.9% walk rate in 39 1/3 frames. O'Brien had 24 saves in his first 28 opportunities. But in 27 appearances after the All-Star break, O'Brien had a 5.11 ERA in 24 2/3 innings, and his walk rate rose to 14.4% while he went 14-for-18 in save chances. Three of his blown saves in the second half came in September, and five of his losing decisions came in his final 13 outings. The 31-year-old said he experienced "fatigue" in the closing days of the season and that his legs have "been feeling heavy compared to how they felt early in the year," according to Daniel Guerrero of the St. Louis Post-Dispatch. As he tired, the velocity of O'Brien's pitches suffered. To be able to maintain velocity through the entire season, O'Brien said he plans to focus on putting on "as much muscle as I can."--Keith Hernandez
Source: St. Louis Post-Dispatch - Daniel Guerrero
Curtis Mead the Favorite to Start at Second Base Next Year


Keith Hernandez




Oct 7, 2026, 11:47 AM ET
Boston Red Sox infielder Curtis Mead is considered the favorite to open next season as the team's starting second baseman, according to Tim Healey of The Boston Globe. The Red Sox acquired Mead from the Washington Nationals at the trade deadline this summer, but he ended up playing in only one game for Boston due to a fractured wrist that he suffered in his second at-bat with the team. The 25-year-old will now have all offseason to heal up, and he will enter spring training as the team's primary option at the keystone as they attempt to get back to the playoffs in 2027. The Australian native was having a breakout 2026 campaign with the Nationals before being traded to Boston, and he finished the year with a .253/.353/.498 slash line with an .851 OPS, 17 home runs, 48 RBI, 49 runs scored, and six stolen bases in 285 at-bats in 88 combined games with Washington and Boston. "That would be, I would say, broadly our plan," said manager Chad Tracy when asked about second base. "He was acquired for a reason. You see the numbers that kind of project at least toward a 30-home run season. And adding that, we were really excited about that."--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Boston Globe - Tim Healey
Walker Buehler to Start Game 4 of NLDS Against Brewers


Keith Hernandez




Oct 7, 2026, 11:36 AM ET
The San Diego Padres announced that veteran right-hander Walker Buehler will make the start in Game 4 of the National League Division Series on Wednesday night at Petco Park against the visiting Milwaukee Brewers. Buehler will make his first postseason appearance this year after going 9-6 with a 4.63 ERA (4.51 FIP) and 1.35 WHIP with 131 strikeouts and 57 walks in 153 2/3 innings pitched across his 32 starts for the Padres in his first season with the team. The 32-year-old is no longer the high-end ace that he was with the Los Angeles Dodgers, but he does have plenty of postseason experience, posting a 3.04 ERA (3.21 FIP) with 114 strikeouts and 36 walks in 94 2/3 innings pitched. Buehler's last start came on Sept. 26 against the division-rival Arizona Diamondbacks, when he allowed four runs (three earned) with a walk and three strikeouts in just 3 2/3 innings for a no-decision. He picked up a win in his only outing against Milwaukee in 2026, giving up just one earned run with two walks and five strikeouts in six innings at Petco Park back on Aug. 11. Buehler will most definitely be on a short leash in a must-win game for San Diego if he is not on his game early on.--Keith Hernandez
Source: Padres PR
Adrian Morejon Dealing With "Stickiness in his Shoulder"


Keith Hernandez




Oct 7, 2026, 11:28 AM ET
San Diego Padres left-handed reliever Adrian Morejon (shoulder) was unavailable in Game 3 of the National League Division Series at Petco Park on Tuesday night against the Milwaukee Brewers due to "stickiness in his shoulder," manager Craig Stammen told AJ Cassavell of MLB.com. There is still a chance that Morejon will be available for Game 4 against the Brewers in San Diego on Wednesday night as the Friars attempt to force a Game 5 back in Milwaukee on Friday night. With Morejon unavailable and closer Mason Miller on the paternity list, the Padres' bullpen was very short on Tuesday night, but Game 1 starter Michael King came to the rescue and threw the final two innings for SD to pick up a save in the 4-3 victory. Morejon has already had two two-inning appearances in this postseason, once in the Wild-Card Series against the Chicago Cubs and again on Saturday against the Brewers in Game of the NLDS, when he allowed the game-winning home run to catcher William Contreras. The hard-throwing Cuban left-hander was one of the most effective late-inning setup men during the regular season, though, going 9-3 with a 2.83 ERA, 1.08 WHIP, three saves, and a career-high 107 strikeouts in just 86 innings out of the bullpen. With Miller unlikely to be back with the team on Wednesday, the Padres could really use Morejon's left arm on Wednesday evening.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com - AJ Cassavell
Oct 6, 2026, 10:58 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers first baseman Freddie Freeman was one of the stars of his team's 3-1 win over the Atlanta Braves in Game 3 of the National League Division Series on Tuesday. Freeman had just one hit in four plate appearances, but it was a solo home run off Braves ace Chris Sale. Freeman put together another strong regular season in 2026, hitting .288/.362/.430 with 16 home runs, 70 RBI, 74 runs scored, and seven stolen bases. The 37-year-old's production tailed off late in the year, as he hit just .184 in September and slugged just one home run across 249 plate appearances after the All-Star break. However, Freeman has looked like his vintage self so far this postseason. Across the first three games of the NLDS, Freeman has logged four hits, two home runs, two RBI, and three runs scored.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 6, 2026, 10:40 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers utility man Enrique Hernandez struck one of the big blows of his team's 3-1 win over the Atlanta Braves in Game 3 of the National League Division Series on Tuesday, clubbing a two-run home run off of Braves ace Chris Sale to open the scoring in the fourth inning. It was Hernandez's only hit of the night, but it helped the Dodgers chase Sale out of the game after just five innings of work. Hernandez missed a large chunk of the regular season with an oblique injury and was not particularly effective when healthy, hitting .222 with four home runs across 96 plate appearances. However, the 35-year-old has a long history as an unlikely postseason hero. Across 332 career plate appearances in the playoffs, Hernandez has now hit .272 with 18 home runs and 44 RBI.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com

After being swept out of last year's NLCS, Pat Murphy and the Milwaukee Brewers look to turn the page in this year's edition with a rematch against the reigning back-to-back champion Los Angeles Dodgers.
Milwaukee heads into the NLCS after defeating the San Diego Padres in the NLDS (3-1), with Los Angeles advancing thanks to its 3-1 series win over the Atlanta Braves.
Find everything you need to know about the series below:
The 2026 MLB postseason has arrived. Stay up to date with the latest results and more.
When is the Dodgers vs. Brewers 2026 MLB NLCS?
The Dodgers and Brewers will begin their best-of-seven series on Sunday, Oct. 11. See the full schedule below.
How to watch Dodgers vs. Brewers: TV channel, live stream
Fans can watch the entire Dodgers-Brewers NLCS on FOX and FS1. Spanish-language coverage will be available on FOX Deportes.
Dodgers vs. Brewers 2026 MLB National League Championship Series full schedule
| Game | Date | Location | Time |
| Game 1 | Sunday, Oct. 11 | American Family Field | TBD |
| Game 2 | Monday, Oct. 12 | American Family Field | TBD |
| Game 3 | Wednesday, Oct. 14 | Dodger Stadium | TBD |
| Game 4 | Thursday, Oct. 15 | Dodger Stadium | TBD |
| Game 5* | Friday, Oct. 16 | Dodger Stadium | TBD |
| Game 6* | Sunday, Oct. 18 | American Family Field | TBD |
| Game 7* | Monday, Oct. 19 | American Family Field | TBD |
* = if necessary
Where will the Dodgers vs. Brewers League Championship Series be played?
Games 1 and 2 will be played in Milwaukee at American Family Field, with Games 3 and 4 moving to Dodger Stadium in Los Angeles. Should the series go past four, Dodger Stadium will host Game 5 before the series heads back to Milwaukee for Games 6 and 7.
Dodgers vs. Brewers probable starting pitchers
Starters for Game 1 and beyond are TBD.
Dodgers vs. Brewers 2026 season series results
The Brewers narrowly finished on top in their season series with the Dodgers, winning four of seven in 2026.
Dodgers vs. Brewers playoff history
The Dodgers and Brewers have met three times in the postseason, where Los Angeles has defeated Milwaukee in each matchup.
- 2025 NLCS: Dodgers win 4-0
- 2020 Wild Card Series: Dodgers win 2-0
- 2018 NLCS: Dodgers win 4-3
How does the MLB League Championship Series format work?
The NLCS and ALCS are best-of-seven series. The higher seed receives home-field advantage for the series, with Games 1-2 and potential Games 6-7 hosted by the higher seed and Games 3-5 hosted by the lower seed. The first team to win four games will take the series and advance to the World Series.

How many games are in the ALCS, NLCS?
The remainder of the MLB postseason will feature best-of-seven series. The higher seed hosts Games 1 and 2, along with the potential Games 6 and 7.

The NLCS begins Sunday, Oct. 11.

The Dodgers will have home-field advantage if they face the Padres. Otherwise, the NLCS will begin in Milwaukee.

item.content:encoded:
The Atlanta Braves are officially on the brink of elimination from the MLB postseason, trailing two games to one in their National League Division Series against the reigning World Series champion Los Angeles Dodgers.
Meanwhile, right fielder Ronald Acuña Jr. recently underwent an MRI after experiencing soreness in his right knee after getting shaken up during a stolen base attempt in their Game 2 win.
The good news for the Braves is that he was given the all-clear and will be in the lineup for Wednesday's elimination contest.
Atlanta Braves Infielder Ronald Acuña Jr. Underwent An MRI
During Game 3 against the Dodgers, Acuña Jr. was originally scheduled to bat second in the order and play right field, but was moved to the designated hitter position because of the lingering soreness in his knee.
He went 0-for-3 with a walk and a strikeout.
The Braves Don't Appear To Be Worried By His Slump
Earlier in the series, the Braves weren't making much of his slump, simply saying they just need him to play to the best of his abilities.
"We just need Ronald to be Ronald," Braves ace Chris Sale said via MLB.com. "I'll be honest, 50 percent of him is better than most. I think going back home might alleviate a little bit of that pressure, being in front of our home fans, and just staying loose. I think you get into these situations, and sometimes you try to do more."
"I don't worry about him just because the talent is so big that it's going to show up," Braves manager Walt Weiss said.
Meanwhile, Acuña Jr. said that he thrives on the pressure.
"I love it when I face the pitchers that are superstars," Acuña said. "Every time I go to the plate to compete. We're trying to win. So I'm doing my best. As you know, these pitches, they're nasty."
The Braves have no choice but to win on Wednesday in order to extend their season.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post Braves' Ronald Acuña Jr. Undergoes MRI appeared first on HEAVY.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] “Zack Wheeler Makes 1 Mistake, All the Sudden I’m the Fool” – Reds Legend Defends His Viral Take Amid Feud With Braves Fans
item.dc:creator: Krutik Jain
item.description: On Tuesday, Cincinnati Reds legend Joey Votto addressed his viral back-and-forth with Atlanta Braves fans after his wrong prediction during the NL Wild Card Series. In the Braves-Phillies Wild Card Game 3 on NBC, Votto predicted that Atlanta would not be able to score any more runs against Philadelphia's Zack Wheeler in the fourth inning. Four pitches later, Ozzie Albies launched a two-run homer, extending Atlanta's lead to 5-0. This sparked a wave of criticism from Braves fans on social media.
item.content:encoded:
On Tuesday, Cincinnati Reds legend Joey Votto addressed his viral back-and-forth with Atlanta Braves fans after his wrong prediction during the NL Wild Card Series. In the Braves-Phillies Wild Card Game 3 on NBC, Votto predicted that Atlanta would not be able to score any more runs against Philadelphia's Zack Wheeler in the fourth inning. Four pitches later, Ozzie Albies launched a two-run homer, extending Atlanta's lead to 5-0. This sparked a wave of criticism from Braves fans on social media. Many of them even concluded that Votto is a Braves hater.
On MLB Now, Votto defended his prediction against the Braves by pointing out that the Phillies ace was pitching really well in that game.
"I made another claim where Zack Wheeler came into the game, and he was throwing incredibly well," Votto said. "He looks so sharp up in the zone, front hip cutter splitter looked great. And as I say, I don't see them getting another run. The one pitch against the guy who had an 80 WRC+ in 2026 against Albies was a middle fastball, and he homered. And I'm happy for him. I love Ozzie Albies, but Zack Wheeler made one mistake, and he gets zinged right away, two runs. And all of a sudden I'm the fool."
Votto sarcastically mentioned the reactions and said his vast experience is the reason he gets paid.
"You don't know what you're talking about," Votto added. "I do. That's why they pay me per game."
Votto also clarified his prediction that the Phillies would come out on top against the Braves, made when Philadelphia scored a run in the first inning against Atlanta's starter Chris Sale in Wild Card Game 1.
"They scored a run in the first inning against Chris Sale," Votto said. "And I said, 'Did they just win the series?' Knowing that 15 of 16 teams that win the first game win the series. That was my logic. The pushback was, 'Oh, it was more like 53 to 56% win probability.' But my answer was, 'Does the win probability actually factor in Luzardo? Does it factor in Duran?' I don't think so. I don't think it does. I think it was plus 60. And my logic was, 'Oh, there's a three-in-five chance that they just won the game now. And if they win this game, 15 of 16 teams.' So I was, of course, being bold."
The Braves ultimately beat Philadelphia 6-2 and advanced to face the Dodgers in the NLDS.
Reds Legend Turns His Back on His Apology to Braves Fan
After receiving severe backlash from the Braves fans, Joey Votto issued an apology on X for predicting against Atlanta twice in the postseason. However, his apology also included another dreadful prediction for the Braves against the Los Angeles Dodgers in the NLDS.
"Braves fans, I want to sincerely apologize for guessing so incorrectly and dismissing your offense. I hear you. Good luck in your next series in Los Angeles," Votto wrote. "Dodgers in 5."
When a Braves fan thanked Votto for the apology, the Reds legend joked:
"I didn't really mean the apology."
As for Votto's NLDS prediction, the Braves are trailing 2-1 in the series against the Dodgers. Votto has predicted that the Dodgers would come out on top in five games. Let's see if the Reds legend's prediction turns out to be right this time.

Yamamoto went seven innings, allowing only o
item.content:encoded:
The Atlanta Braves enter Game 4 of the NLDS with their season on the line after falling behind 2-1 in the series against the Los Angeles Dodgers.
Atlanta was fortunate to split the first two games at Dodger Stadium before they dropped Game 3 at Truist Park. Now facing elimination, there is more pressure than ever for the Braves' offense to break through.
The Braves' offense struggled mightily in Game 3 against 2025 World Series MVP Yoshinobu Yamamoto. Yamamoto went seven innings, allowing only one run and recording 10 strikeouts. The Braves would go on to record only one hit over the following two innings against Tanner Scott and Edwin Diaz.
Atlanta has yet to score more than three runs in the series, but the team's biggest bats will need to deliver on Wednesday against right-hander Tyler Glasnow. Braves third baseman Austin Riley is one of the hitters still trying to find his footing in the series.
No Panic in Atlanta
Riley, a two-time All-Star, is 0-for-10 with five strikeouts through the first three games of the series. Despite facing elimination and his own struggles at the plate, Riley is not panicking ahead of a critical Game 4.
"We're still very confident. It's a confident clubhouse. We think we can get the job done and take this thing to LA. We've just got to go out there and play clean baseball and capitalize on the opportunities when it presents itself," Riley said, according to Barrett Sallee of the Braves Radio Network.
Riley's confidence will need to translate into results immediately if the Braves are to keep their season alive. The Braves cannot afford to waste scoring chances against a Dodgers pitching staff that has controlled the majority of this series.
Far From His Best
Sep 29, 2026; Cumberland, Georgia, USA; Atlanta Braves third baseman Austin Riley (27) reacts after hitting a three run home run against the Philadelphia Phillies in the eighth inning during game one of the Wildcard round for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Truist Park. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)
Riley's difficult series at the plate comes following his worst statistical season of his career. In 159 games this year, he is slashing .219/.290/.364 for a career-worst .654 OPS with 19 home runs and 72 RBIs.
Despite a challenging year, Riley has shown flashes of his All-Star self this postseason. In Game 1 of the Wild Card Series against the Philadelphia Phillies, Riley hit a three-run, go-ahead home run in the eighth inning to flip the momentum Atlanta's way en route to a Game 1 victory.
With the Braves on the brink of elimination, Wednesday's Game 4 would be a perfect time for another one of those game-changing moments.

item.dc:creator: Justin Binkowski; Unknown
item.description: Following a heroic relief appearance by San Diego Padres right-hander Michael King, baseball fans will be treated to another day of four Division Series games on Wednesday. The Los Angeles Dodgers beat the Atlanta Braves 3-1 on Tuesday, while the Padres kept their postseason hopes alive with a 4-3 victory over the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 3 of the National League Division Series. All four teams will be back in action on Wednesday, with San Diego and Atlanta needing a win to stay in the 2026 MLB
item.content:encoded:
Following a heroic relief appearance by San Diego Padres right-hander Michael King, baseball fans will be treated to another day of four Division Series games on Wednesday.
The Los Angeles Dodgers beat the Atlanta Braves 3-1 on Tuesday, while the Padres kept their postseason hopes alive with a 4-3 victory over the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 3 of the National League Division Series. All four teams will be back in action on Wednesday, with San Diego and Atlanta needing a win to stay in the 2026 MLB playoffs.
Here are the expected starting pitching matchups for Game 4 in each NLDS.
Braves vs. Dodgers
Los Angeles right-hander Yoshinobu Yamamoto delivered another dominant postseason performance on Tuesday, tossing seven innings of one-run ball and striking out 10. With a 2-1 series lead, the Dodgers will now give the ball to another All-Star hurler.
Right-hander Tyler Glasnow will start for Los Angeles in Game 4. The 6-foot-8 righty will make his first playoff appearance of the season on Wednesday after being limited to 13 regular-season starts. But the hard-throwing hurler still had a 3.53 ERA and 98 strikeouts in 74 innings this year. In his career, the 33-year-old has a 4.43 ERA in 16 postseason games (13 starts).
With Atlanta's season on the line, right-hander Tyler Mahle is starting Game 4. The 32-year-old made his MLB postseason debut in the Braves' Wild Card Series matchup with the Philadelphia Phillies, throwing seven innings and allowing just one run. The veteran will try to keep the Dodgers' bats at bay to force a winner-take-all Game 5.
Brewers vs. Padres
With the Padres facing elimination, King pitched the last two innings of Game 3 after starting Game 2. Relievers Mason Miller and Adrian Morejon were unavailable on Tuesday, so Robbie Ray and Joe Musgrove were warming up in the bullpen during the ninth inning of Game 3. With that in mind, San Diego will likely have all hands on deck in Game 4.
The Padres will start right-hander Walker Buehler on Wednesday. The 32-year-old has plenty of postseason experience, posting a 3.04 ERA in 19 career playoff games. But it'll be interesting to see how long of a leash the veteran has in a must-win game for San Diego.
Meanwhile, left-hander Robert Gasser is expected to start Game 4 for the Brewers. The 27-year-old will make his first postseason start after pitching in two games out of the bullpen in the 2025 playoffs. Most notably, though, Gasser starting on Wednesday sets the stage for Jacob Misiorowski to either pitch in the late innings of Game 4 or start Game 5 for Milwaukee if necessary.
Justin Binkowski is a lifelong baseball fan returning to cover the sport he loves after spending nearly a decade writing about video games. Before his time as managing editor at Dot Esports, Binkowski attended King's College in Wilkes-Barre, PA, where he was also a relief pitcher on the school's baseball team. While in college, Binkowski was a media relations intern for the Scranton/Wilkes-Barre RailRiders during the 2014 season.

item.title: [MLB.com] Turang, Yelich key to Crew wrapping up NLDS
item.dc:creator: Mark Sheldon
item.description: SAN DIEGO -- It sure felt like forever since Christian Yelich notched a postseason RBI. And it was way too long before Brice Turang got his first hit against the Padres in this National League Division Series. Still, the Brewers will need to get more from both players to help them advance to the next round, and perhaps beyond, after being handed a 4-3 loss in Tuesday's Game 3 as the Padres stayed alive for another day and now trail, 2-1, in the best-of-five series. One of several missed opportun
item.content:encoded:
SAN DIEGO -- It sure felt like forever since Christian Yelich notched a postseason RBI. And it was way too long before Brice Turang got his first hit against the Padres in this National League Division Series.
Still, the Brewers will need to get more from both players to help them advance to the next round, and perhaps beyond, after being handed a 4-3 loss in Tuesday's Game 3 as the Padres stayed alive for another day and now trail, 2-1, in the best-of-five series.
One of several missed opportunities for Milwaukee came in the fifth inning. The Brewers had already scored a tying run and then had the bases loaded and two outs when Turang grounded softly to shortstop Xander Bogaerts for a fielder's choice to keep from adding on.
"Trying to get a good pitch to hit. Just didn’t work out," Turang said. "It’s all right. We’ve got to move on and go win tomorrow."
That out made Turang 0-for-10 in the series and 2-for-40 (.050) with 14 strikeouts over his last 11 postseason games. The hitless skid ended when he lofted a two-out single to left field just out of reach for a diving Jase Bowen in the seventh inning.
"I’ve hit some balls right to people and had some good at-bats. I’ve just got to keep working, keep pushing forward," Turang said. "You just want to get better every day."
Yelich, the recently minted team captain and Milwaukee's longest-tenured star, picked up Turang by scorching a 107.2 mph liner to left-center field for an RBI single. It was his first RBI in a playoff game since his first-inning home run in Game 7 of the 2018 NL Championship Series vs. the Dodgers in a losing effort.
Both hitters got another chance to come through for Milwaukee in the top of the ninth inning. Turang worked a walk against Padres pitcher Michael King to put runners on first and second base with one out.
Yelich followed by blistering a first-pitch slider from King at 107.1 mph, only to see it one-hop directly to Bogaerts at shortstop, who turned the game-ending double play.
"A step to the right or left, it's pretty good," Yelich said. "I hit it hard. Just happened to be right at them. It's unfortunate. Part of the game. It's just how it goes sometimes. You've just got to keep battling. Not much else you can do. It is frustrating when it doesn't really bounce your way, but that's how it goes."
Although he’s driven in just the one run in this series, Yelich is batting .400 (4-for-10) with a double. He got the Brewers' first hit in all three games, and in the Game 2 thriller he drew a one-out walk that led to Jackson Chourio's two-run, walk-off single.
"He's looked great," Brewers hitting coach Eric Theisen said. "He's been on time. He's had some hard contact. As a team, we've had hard contact and some loud outs."
As for Turang, he was the Major League leader for September in average (.361) and on-base percentage (.475) before hitting the schneid in October.
"I think he's working his process, same as he always does, working his ABs," Theisen said. "We've seen some good swings. We've seen him put together some good ABs. The results haven't come. But he's continuing to work day to day the same way he always does. I still think he's in a good spot. Keep plugging away."
Sometimes a hit -- even a soft one -- can break the spell, but Theisen didn't put too much stock in Turang's bloop single.
"It's great that the ball falls and you get a knock and get on base. But the pitch-to-pitch approach and the way he's navigating at-bats is what's important," Theisen said. "The process is what's important."
Milwaukee left 11 men on base and missed multiple opportunities to take control of the game that would have given them an NLDS sweep. Besides Turang and Yelich, Chourio went 0-for-4 with a fifth-inning sacrifice fly. He was robbed of a hit by center fielder Jackson Merrill's great catch on the warning track to open the game. Bauers went 0-for-4 with four strikeouts and a walk.
"We had some really good at-bats, hit the ball hard, put ourselves in a good position to win the game. Sometimes you just need that big hit. We’ve got to focus on winning tomorrow," Turang said. "The quality of at-bats that we’ve had has been really cool to see. We’ll get it going. I trust everybody in this locker room."
Said Theisen: "Not everybody's been hot all year long, and it seems like the lineup is deep. When one or two guys have a stretch of games or two or three where maybe they're not producing like they always do, somebody steps up and does it. That's the beautiful thing about this offense and what we've shown all year."
Now the Brewers need to show it in Game 4.

item.content:encoded:
The 2026 MLB playoffs have arrived!
The 12-team postseason began with an action-packed wild-card round that featured eight teams battling for four spots to advance to the eight-team division series.
The Chicago White Sox became the first team to win a series this postseason with a wild-card round sweep of the Houston Astros. Then the New York Yankees swept the Boston Red Sox in two routs, recording the highest series run differential in the history of the current wild-card format. The San Diego Padresalso sealed their spot in the NLDS with a sweep of the Chicago Cubs. In the only wild-card series to go the distance, the Atlanta Braves held off the Philadelphia Philliesto move on.
From the first pitch of the wild-card games to the last out of the World Series, we've got you covered with the postseason bracket, schedules, results and how to watch every game this October.

item.content:encoded:
How Braves' Ronald Acuna Jr. has impressed analyst despite quiet playoffs showing appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Atlanta Braves won the 2021 World Series without Ronald Acuna Jr., but they are unlikely to go all the way in 2026 unless the franchise pillar comes alive in the playoffs. He was hitting just .167 with a .485 OPS through his last 18 at-bats entering Tuesday's National League Division Series battle versus the Los Angeles Dodgers. One broadcaster is not worried, however.
"He's been okay in the postseason — he hasn't been the superstar yet — but we feel like his moment is coming. Sooner than later," Braves color analyst C.J. Nitkowski told the "Foul Territory" podcast. "The thing I have been impressed with is he's not necessarily become a guy who's pressing. There are times you're watching at-bats and you know he wants to do something big, and you're thinking 'man, he's going to chase here.' And he doesn't.
"He's been under control. It hasn't happened for him just yet… but nobody's worried about the health of Ronald Acuna Jr. {or} his ability to put up big moments here in the postseason."
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Ronald Acuña Jr. has wisely avoided pressing in big moments, and it's caught @CJNitkowski's eye…
"He hasn't been the superstar yet, but we feel like his moment is coming sooner rather than later." pic.twitter.com/AJSdOfJVi1
— Foul Territory (@FoulTerritoryTV) October 6, 2026
Players live and die by their approach in this sport, and if their process proves successful, the hits will come. The prodigiously talented Acuna believes he will deliver for the Braves when they need him most. Former MVP Award winners tend to be confident, and for good reason. He eventually erupted in the regular season, and fans are trusting him to do the same in October.
Acuna has endured his struggles during this time of the year, however. He owns a .769 OPS through 34 playoff games, which is nearly 130 points lower than his career output. That still might be enough to help Atlanta move forward.
The 28-year-old right fielder is eying his first extra-base hit of the 2026 postseason during a pivotal Game 3 NLDS clash. Ronald Acuna Jr. is still finding ways to contribute, scoring a run in his four previous games, but one big knock could open the flood gates in Truist Park.

item.content:encoded:
Ronald Acuña Jr. is dealing with right knee soreness.

Acuña appeared to suffer the injury when he slid feet-first into second on a stolen base attempt during Game 2 in Los Angeles. The 28-year-old franchise cornerstone remains in Atlanta’s lineup at DH to face Dodgers ace Yoshinobu Yamamoto in Game 3 at Truist Park on Wednesday evening. It’ll be Lane Thomas heading out to take his spot in right field. It doesn’t appear to be a significant concern, but the Braves clearly aren’t going to take any chances by exposing him to additional wear and tear from a defensive standpoint that would jeopardize his availability moving forward in the postseason.

item.title: [MLB.com] Rays-Yankees ALDS Game 3 FAQ (Wed., 8 p.m. ET, TBS/HBO Max)
item.dc:creator: Adam Berry; Bryan Hoch
item.description: NEW YORK -- Two weeks ago, the Rays went wild in the visitors’ clubhouse at Yankee Stadium after clinching their first American League East championship in five years. That party started shortly after a win over the Yankees and carried late into the New York night. Could they have another celebration in store in the Bronx? It’s time for the American League Division Series to shift venues, going from the Rays’ home dome at Tropicana Field to Yankee Stadium for Game 3 on Wednesday night. But the R
item.content:encoded:
NEW YORK -- Two weeks ago, the Rays went wild in the visitors’ clubhouse at Yankee Stadium after clinching their first American League East championship in five years. That party started shortly after a win over the Yankees and carried late into the New York night.
Could they have another celebration in store in the Bronx?
It’s time for the American League Division Series to shift venues, going from the Rays’ home dome at Tropicana Field to Yankee Stadium for Game 3 on Wednesday night. But the Rays are still right where they want to be, holding a commanding 2-0 lead in the series with three chances to advance to the AL Championship Series.
“It's amazing, man. It's exactly the way we wanted to start the series,” Rays closer Bryan Baker said. “To be able to play in front of these fans in this building and take a 2-0 series lead was exactly what we wanted, so it feels really good right now.”
Maybe home-field advantage is what the Yankees need after coming up empty against Rays ace Drew Rasmussen in Game 1 and kicking the ball around the infield in a mistake-filled Game 2 defeat. Or maybe it’ll help to send left-hander Max Fried to the mound, knowing how tough he’s been on Tampa Bay throughout his career.
“We've got to get over it,” Yankees manager Aaron Boone said after Game 2. “We've responded all year to difficult times, and we've got to do that again. We've got to get ourselves up off the mat.”
Tampa Bay’s pitching staff held what looked like a red-hot New York lineup to only two runs in the first 18 innings of this series. If the Rays keep that up, they could enjoy another champagne-soaked night in the city that never sleeps.
“I think it's sweet either way. Doesn't matter the clubhouse,” Rays center fielder Jonny DeLuca said. “Obviously, going over there, having the chance to do that would be pretty special.”
When is the game and how can I watch it?
First pitch for Game 3 of the Yankees-Rays Division Series is set for 8 p.m. ET on Wednesday at Yankee Stadium. The game will be broadcast on TBS, truTV and HBO Max.
The ALDS will be available in Spanish on UniMas, while Univision’s TUDN Radio will provide Spanish-language audio coverage. ESPN Radio will provide live national coverage of all 2026 MLB Postseason games.
Who are the starting pitchers?
Rays: Nick Martinez, RHP
Key stats: 7-3, 2.38 ERA in 16 road starts this season
After rolling out Rasmussen in Game 1 and Freddy Peralta in Game 2, Martinez was the logical choice for the Rays with the series moving to the Bronx. The veteran right-hander was a reliable presence on the mound for Tampa Bay all season, as he posted a 3.10 ERA over 180 innings while the club went 22-9 in his starts. He was at his best on the road, including two outings in the Bronx. The first-time All-Star held the Yankees to only three runs over 12 innings in their home ballpark.
Yankees: Max Fried, LHP
Key stats: 5-1, 1.81 ERA in 7 career GS vs. Tampa Bay
Fried is coming off a sharp outing against the Red Sox in the decisive Game 2 of the AL Wild Card Series, holding Boston to a run on three hits over six innings. Fried walked one and struck out six, his third postseason start since joining the Yankees.
This will be Fried’s third time facing the Rays this season. He last saw them on Sept. 22 in New York, taking the loss in a 6 2/3-inning effort as Tampa Bay clinched the AL East.
Fried also went up against the Rays on April 11 at Tropicana Field, taking a no-decision after permitting three runs over eight innings. For his career, Fried is 5-1 with a 1.81 ERA in seven starts vs. Tampa Bay, including 3-0 with a 0.84 ERA in three starts during the 2025 season.
What might the starting lineups look like?
Rays: It seems likely the Rays will change things up a bit against the Yankees’ left-handers, opting for the right-handed side of most platoons and leaving their lefty hitters available off the bench. Here’s one potential look for a more right-handed lineup.
Yankees: The Yankees have used the same lefty-heavy lineup three times this postseason against right-handed pitchers, including twice in the ALDS. Boone said he is considering shaking things up for Game 3. Boone said before Game 2 that he was considering starting Anthony Volpe at third base. Jose Caballero and Paul Goldschmidt could also enter the mix.
How will the bullpens line up after the starter?
Rays: The Rays really couldn’t be in much better shape thanks to their starting rotation. Rasmussen handled eight innings in Game 1, and the duo of Peralta and Ian Seymour combined to work 7 2/3 innings in Game 2. So, their traditional relievers have recorded seven of the 54 outs so far this series: six from Baker and a big one from lefty Cam Booser. They may not turn to Peralta or Seymour in Game 3, but they still have starter Griffin Jax available -- and the Yankees have yet to face setup men Tyler Wells and Kevin Kelly in this series.
Yankees: Ryan Weathers replaced infielder/outfielder Amed Rosario for this series, returning from a left flexor strain sustained in late August. David Bednar, Paul Blackburn and Brent Headrick should all be leaned upon for high-leverage outs. Will Warren is now in the bullpen after appearing in 32 games (29 starts) during the regular season. Warren made one appearance in the Wild Card Series, tossing 1 2/3 innings.
Any injuries of note?
Rays: Nothing new. Everyone who was expected to be available for this series is on the roster. The most notable injury situation to watch moving forward is that of left-hander Shane McClanahan, whose status is unclear except that he will not pitch in this series.
Yankees: Aaron Judge was left off the ALDS roster, though Boone said it was a “close” call. Judge has yet to run the bases as he recovers from a right calf strain, though he has been performing outfield running. He has also been taking numerous live at-bats while throwing. Clarke Schmidt has been ruled out for the remainder of the postseason.
Who is hot and who is not?
Rays: Aranda doesn’t get as much love as the other members of the “Big Three,” but his left-handed bat is key. He hit better than either Caminero or Díaz in September, and he had the lone big hit of the night in Game 1 before picking up two more hits in Game 2. Richie Palacios finished strong, too, posting a .981 OPS with five homers in September before delivering the biggest hit of Game 2, and the Brooklyn native likes hitting against his hometown Yankees. Tampa Bay’s entire rotation surged into the postseason, highlighted by Rasmussen and Peralta, the September AL Pitcher of the Month.
The Rays’ outfield is off to a slow start in this series, offensively, but they all showed the impact they can have by putting the ball in play in Game 2. And their defense has been consistently excellent.
Yankees: Rice has been the Yankees' most productive hitter in the postseason, and given how the ALDS has gone, it hasn't been particularly close. Rice is 7-for-15 (.467) in the playoffs, including his two-homer performance in ALDS Game 2. Rice has four homers and eight RBIs overall. Wells is 5-for-12 (.417) in the playoffs, including a couple of doubles in the ALDS. Everyone except for Rice and Wells has combined to go 1-for-46 (.022) in the ALDS so far.
Anything else fans might want to know?
• The Yankees won four of the six games these clubs played in the Bronx during the regular season, splitting a pair of games in late May, then taking three of four the final week of the season. However, the Rays have already celebrated once at Yankee Stadium, as they clinched the AL East title with a 6-1 win in the second half of a doubleheader on Sept. 22.

item.content:encoded:
The National League’s top-seeded Milwaukee Brewers head to San Diego, California, with a 2-0 lead in their NLDS matchup against the Padres for Game 3 Tuesday night at Petco Park. The Brewers have a chance to advance to the NLCS for the second consecutive year with a win, while the Padres will be fighting to keep their season alive with the help of their home crowd.
The Brewers earned a first-round bye as the No. 1 seed in the NL and home-field advantage throughout the MLB playoffs after finishing the regular season with the best record in the league. While that extra time off during the Wild Card Series has hurt teams with a first-round bye plenty of times in the past, it hasn’t slowed down Milwaukee, which won the first two games of the NLDS against San Diego.
Both games have been one-run contests so far, with Brewers catcher William Contreras playing the hero in Game 1 with his go-ahead solo home run in the seventh inning as Milwaukee went on to win 3-2. The Brewers followed that with a dramatic 4-3 victory in Game 2 when 22-year-old outfielder Jackson Chourio delivered a walk-off two-RBI single against Padres superstar closer Mason Miller.
The Brewers are giving the start to right-hander Dustin May for Game 3. May went 7-9 with a 4.70 ERA across 31 regular season starts between Milwaukee and St. Louis. Tuesday night will be May’s first playoff appearance since he appeared in seven games with the Los Angeles Dodgers in 2020.
The Padres will counter with right-hander Nick Pivetta, who missed a large portion of the season due to injury before making his return on Sept. 7. He posted a 2-0 record with a 1.45 ERA across four starts in September and has pitched really well for San Diego since signing with the team ahead of the 2025 season, owning a 16-7 record with a 2.87 ERA and 0.99 WHIP over the last two regular seasons. Pivetta already made a start for the Padres in the NL Wild Card Series, allowing one run over 3.1 innings against the Chicago Cubs on Sept. 30.
Check out Brewers vs. Padres MLB playoff predictions, picks, and more below ahead of Tuesday night’s NLDS Game 3 at Petco Park.

- Total (Runs): Over 7.5 (-110), Under 7.5 (-110)

Brewers vs. Padres MLB Playoff Predictions
Don’t forget to check out the Stats Hub at Hard Rock Bet Sportsbook, where you can find our Brewers vs. Padres MLB playoff prediction below, which uses baseball betting insights and trends to support the pick:
Padres vs. Brewers Best Bet: Fernando Tatís Jr. Over 0.5 Runs (-105)
Fernando Tatís Jr. is the tone-setter at the top of the Padres’ lineup, and when a dynamic player like him who’s a major threat on the base paths reaches safely, there’s a good chance he’ll end up coming around to score. Tatís’ 96 runs scored during the regular season were near the top of MLB, and while it’s still a small sample size, his four runs scored during the playoffs so far are tied for the second-most.
Tatís is batting only .176 this postseason, but he has a stolen base and has scored the four runs mentioned above. He scored three runs in the Padres’ Game 1 win over the Cubs in the NL Wild Card Series and then scored a run in Game 2 of the NLDS this past Sunday. Tatís has also scored at least one run in three of his last five games dating back to the regular season.

item.title: [BoSox Injection] MLB silently confirms Yankees fans whining about Sonny Gray cheating were wasting their time
item.dc:creator: Katie Manganelli
item.description: Sonny Gray pitched a great game against the New York Yankees in Wild Card Game 2. Chad Tracy pulled him in the fifth inning despite the single run he'd allowed at that point and the Boston Red Sox crumbled from there. During the game, some fans noticed some brown flecks on the right side of Gray's neck, on the same side as his pitching arm. item.content:encoded:
Sonny Gray pitched a great game against the New York Yankees in Wild Card Game 2. Chad Tracy pulled him in the fifth inning despite the single run he'd allowed at that point and the Boston Red Sox crumbled from there.
During the game, some fans noticed some brown flecks on the right side of Gray's neck, on the same side as his pitching arm. Speculation about cheating ran rampant on social media despite the veteran passing all his in-game hand and glove checks from the umpires.
Chris Cotillo on October 6 reported that MLB investigated Gray for the potential use of illegal substances. Since Gray has not been officially disciplined by the league and he passed all the in-game examinations, Cotillo assumes he's in the clear.
While it was evident that Gray had something on his neck, it didn't look like pine tar, which can be seen in dark, glossy layers on players' helmets and bats. in April 2024, Yankees pitcher Michael Pineda was ejected for using pine tar, which he rubbed on his neck before the game, to improve his grip on the ball. The pine tar was in a uniform smear on his neck and not pilled up, as whatever was on Gray's neck appeared.
MLB investigated Red Sox's Sonny Gray for rumors of illegal sticky substance use in Wild Card Game 2 against Yankees
If there was something sticky on Gray's neck that remained there after he rubbed his fingers over it before nearly every batter, it would remain on his hands when he presented them to umpires to be checked after every inning.
It wasn't even unique for Gray to touch his neck before every pitch — he's been seen doing the same swiping motion on the side of his neck countless times. Using sweat to increase the stickiness of rosin on one's hands, a completely legal substance, is a trick used by pitchers throughout the league over many years.
Gray was the Sox's ace all season and he gave his teammates a great start in the postseason without cheating. His 2.72 ERA over 169 innings this season and 1.98 ERA in two starts against the Yankees aren't indicative of someone who needs extra, illegal help to get through games.
Gray is an impending free agent and the Sox's 2027 rotation will miss him dearly. He was the only righty in the rotation and his 18 wins matched Garrett Crochet's total in 2025. Both pitchers were incredibly effective stoppers in their full seasons with Boston.
Gray's tenure with the Red Sox didn't end on the best note, as he was dissatisfied with Tracy's decision to pull him so early in the game. But if Boston seeks a reunion with Gray, it can do so in good conscience, knowing he didn't use illegal substances in a playoff game.
